1.Nf3 Nf6 2.c4 c6 3.b3 d5 4.Bb2 Bg4 5.e3.strategy: Opens the f1-bishop's diagonal and prepares quick development. If Black trades on f3, the queen recaptures without damaging White's pawns. A solid, flexible answer that keeps the centre in reserve and leaves it to Black to decide whether to trade the bishop.
1.Nf3 Nf6 2.c4 c6 3.b3 d5 4.Bb2 Bg4 5.e3.name: Réti Opening: Anglo-Slav Variation, Capablanca Variation

1.Nf3 Nf6 2.c4 c6 3.b3 d5 4.Bb2 Bg4 5.d3.strategy: Keeps the e-pawn flexible and supports a later central advance, but the pawn on d3 shuts the f1-bishop's diagonal, so that piece can come out only to e2 or after a kingside fianchetto. A modest set-up that develops more slowly than the alternative.
